subject: NexuBank follow-up: prioritized eval pack, prompts, and rollback criteria
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@nexubank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: NexuBank follow-up: prioritized eval pack, prompts, and rollback criteria

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up a focused sandbox run: 

1) Summary of what we heard from your team
- Primary product flow: automated transaction classification + customer support summarization for disputed transactions.
- Top concerns: hallucination in summaries, false positives on fraud-y classification, and predictable latency under 300ms p50 for single-turn API calls.
- Compliance: must keep logs for 90 days and support audit tracebacks.

2) Recommended models to evaluate (prioritized)
- redwood-gen-13b-rlhf-v2 (baseline for high-fidelity summarization)
- redwood-lite-8k-quant-v3 (cost-optimized variant, quantized; good throughput for classification)
- redwood-legacy-7b-v1 (compatibility check; useful as a rollback candidate if newer variants introduce drift)

3) What I attached / included in the eval pack
- nexubank-eval-pack-v1.zip (benchmarks, labeled testset of 1,200 transactions, test harness config)
- nexubank-prompts.csv (example prompt sets: two-shot classification, summarization templates, safety filters)
- benchmarks-nexubank-2028-04.pdf (latency/cost matrix and token-level profiles)

4) Key metrics we will track in the first run
- Classification F1 (label-level, target > 0.92)
- Summarization hallucination rate (manual sample + automatic hallucination detector)
- Token-level p50/p95 latency (target p50 < 300ms; p95 < 600ms)
- Token cost per 1k tokens (estimated with batching)

5) Mitigation / rollback options if we observe regression
- Immediate: pin traffic to a known-good model snapshot (recommended: redwood-legacy-7b-v1 snapshot 2028-03-28)
- Canary: staged rollout to redwood-gen-13b-rlhf-v2 at 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated checks at each step
- Escalation: capture 200 samples from failing requests and run them through our offline diff harness; if hallucination delta > 3% absolute, trigger rollback.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the two priority test cases (classification + summarization) and provide a small sample of representative PSRs (production sample requests) for seeding the eval harness.
- We run the sandbox evaluation (estimated 24–36 hrs) and share a one-page ops summary + detailed diff report.
- If you want contractual guardrails, we can add a service-level pin clause to the SOW to mandate model-pinning during production upgrades.

I pasted a short extract of the benchmark matrix below and included links to the dashboard.

Example latency/cost (from our staging profile with 1k token average):
- redwood-gen-13b-rlhf-v2: p50=420ms, p95=830ms, est cost= $24 / 1M tokens
- redwood-lite-8k-quant-v3: p50=180ms, p95=420ms, est cost= $11 / 1M tokens
- redwood-legacy-7b-v1: p50=260ms, p95=560ms, est cost= $15 / 1M tokens

Link to live dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/NXB-049/dashboard

If you want, Marissa can run through the eval pack in a short 20-minute focused session tomorrow or Wednesday.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Sean — useful summary. A couple quick asks before we kick off: 
- Can you break out the latency/cost numbers by single-request vs batched inference? We expect to run both patterns in production.
- Please share a one-page regression checklist we can review internally (legal and ops like to see triggers).
- I reviewed the prompts attachment; can you confirm whether the hallucination detector is an automated metric or a manual sample check?

I can provide a 200-transaction sample from our QA stream by EOD Wednesday. Procurement wants a high-level SOW and pricing estimate to circulate.

Jordan

Subject: Re: NexuBank follow-up: prioritized eval pack, prompts, and rollback criteria

Jordan — quick answers inline and a short checklist below.

- Latency/cost by pattern:
  • Single-request (no batching): redwood-gen-13b-rlhf-v2 p50=420ms / est cost $28 / 1M; redwood-lite-8k-quant-v3 p50=190ms / est cost $14 / 1M.
  • Batching (batch size = 8 typical): redwood-gen-13b-rlhf-v2 p50=210ms / est cost $18 / 1M; redwood-lite-8k-quant-v3 p50=95ms / est cost $7 / 1M.

- Hallucination detector: hybrid approach
  • Automated: token-overlap heuristics + entailment model that flags likely hallucinations (gives an estimated hallucination score per response).
  • Manual: we also run a 200-sample manual review for high-sensitivity flows (we recommend this for your first run).

Regression checklist (one-pager summary we will attach to SOW):
1) Baseline capture: record 1,200 labeled transactions (we included 1,200 in the eval pack)
2) Key metrics & thresholds: classification F1 drop > 0.03 absolute OR summarization hallucination delta > 0.03 absolute triggers review
3) Canary plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic ramp with automated gating (4-hour observation windows)
4) Rollback policy: immediate pin to snapshot if gate fails; snapshot recommended: redwood-legacy-7b-v1@2028-03-28
5) Audit artifacts: include request/response IDs, model snapshot ids, and 200 failing samples saved to S3 for offline diffing
6) Communication: Ops alert + weekly short status to product + legal notification if regression impacts PII handling

Operational note on pinning: pinning holds a route to a model snapshot; it is reversible but requires an ops approval for unpinning. We can include a contractual pin clause in the SOW that requires 48 hours notice and a joint sign-off for major version upgrades.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will schedule the sandbox run once you confirm the sample and procurement has the SOW draft. Karthik will prepare a short canary gating script (open-source snippet) we can share.

I attached a formal regression checklist PDF to this reply (see attachments in thread top).

—
Sean
